item.title: Preserving Utility in Continual LLM Unlearning via Orthogonal Projections
item.description:
This research tackles the problem of repeatedly removing sensitive data from a large language model without losing performance. The authors built Continual Orthogonal Projection (COP), a simple gradient‑projection method that keeps each deletion orthogonal to previous ones, so utility stays high and forgetting stays strong. Experiments on standard benchmarks show COP outperforms existing continual‑unlearning techniques.

IT Breakdown: If you manage cloud‑hosted LLMs, here is what to do: 1) add COP’s low‑rank basis cache to your inference pipeline; 2) whenever a deletion request arrives, run a single gradient step constrained to COP’s orthogonal subspace; 3) monitor utility metrics to confirm no drift. If your org uses continual data deletion, check that your current unlearning routine isn’t causing interference between successive requests.

item.title: [News] Spooky New Infostealer Malware Uses AI to ‘Autodox’ Victims
item.description: Cisco Talos has identified a new AI‑enhanced infostealer called Volta‑Autodoxer that automatically profiles victims and prioritizes credential theft using large language models. The malware can harvest tokens, passwords, and personal data, then feed the findings to LLMs for rapid analysis, raising the threat level for enterprise security stacks.

item.title: [News] How a Contractor’s Claude Agent Got Into the Pentagon
item.description: A defense contractor integrated Anthropic’s Claude AI into a secure Department of Defense system, raising concerns about potential security gaps in sensitive environments. The incident underscores the need for tighter AI governance and monitoring across all secure IT infrastructures.

item.title: [News] Anthropic VS code extension on Cursor backdoored for nearly 12 hours
item.description: A malicious version (2.1.313) of Anthropic’s Claude VS Code extension was distributed through Cursor’s marketplace, enabling a persistent SSH backdoor on up to 5,000 developer machines. The attack exploited the official distribution channel and left users vulnerable to credential theft and remote access without their knowledge.

item.title: [News] Meta’s Muse Could Upend All Kinds of Businesses. It Hasn’t Yet
item.description: Meta’s new agentic AI tool, Muse, is gaining traction among consumers for online shopping, with over 10 million users in the US and Canada and partnerships with major retailers like Walmart and Best Buy. The tool’s early adoption is prompting businesses to optimize their websites for agent interactions and monitor potential impacts on brand loyalty and pricing strategy.

item.title: [News] Tell HN: Scribd Breached
item.description: Scribd, Inc. disclosed a security incident involving an unauthorized third party accessing user data, as reported on October 26, 2026. The breach potentially exposes sensitive documents and media across Scribd's platforms, including Slideshare and Everand.
